fences.description: Hybrid code dogfoods the customer surface: portal, CLI, and observability-UI code may not path-dep substrate crates. Reach the platform through the public surface (forge-sdk-v2, the HTTP APIs) instead. Escapes are legal with a named reason — every escape is a discovered gap in the customer surface, and the escape log is the customer-harness backlog.

gates.description: rustfmt must be clean whenever Rust sources change. Enable only on a tree that is already fmt-clean — a gate that lands red hides everything behind it (forge-cli lesson). Promoted from hybrid local on second consumer (substrate).

Compile first, run second. `cargo check -p <owning closure>` on every edit catches most of what an edit breaks in seconds; the test suite stays at pre-done where it has the wall clock to finish. Before this, post-edit's only Rust gate fleet-wide was cargo-fmt — an edit that did not compile was not discovered until the agent said it was done.

The repo's own cargo test suite must be green before completion is accepted or a commit lands. Session-local tier of "tests green" — heavier suites (e2e, cross-repo) bind at the merge boundary instead (D-010). Promoted from hybrid local/portal-tests on second consumer (substrate).
Consumers may quarantine a flaky test in `.harness/quarantine.json`, a list of `{test, since, reason, issue?}`. Quarantined tests are skipped at pre-done/pre-commit and RUN in the CI sweep, so the loop stops paying for a known-flaky test without the escape rate going blind; entries older than 14 days are named on stderr. Every skip, retry and flaky pass is in `details`.
On a red, `details.failures` names the tests that failed and carries a bounded tail of each one's output, plus an excerpt of the run for the reds that have no failing test at all (a compile error). Counts alone sent two adjudications of the same failure back to re-run the suite just to learn its name.

Fails when a generated artifact is uncommitted. CI checks out the COMMITTED tree and runs the drift gate against it, so an emitted file left dirty is a red build that no local check can see — `self-check` compares the lockfile against DISK, which is clean in exactly this case.
Written after a fleet roll staged `.harness`, `.github` and `.gitignore` by hand and missed `.claude/settings.json#hooks`, across thirteen repos. The verification used the same hand-typed list, so it confirmed the blind spot instead of catching it. The lockfile already records what was emitted; this gate reads it rather than remembering.

Targeted local e2e tier (D-019): when a session's changed paths touch surfaces the consumer's e2e-map.json declares coverage for, the matching Playwright specs run against the LOCAL dev platform at pre-done. The full suite stays at the merge boundary (CI dispatch, D-010) — this tier exists so e2e-visible regressions surface at the session boundary, not a merge later. Paths with no mapping pass with that fact recorded; a matched path with the platform down is an infrastructure error (never a silent pass) — boot dev/up.sh or use WIP mode.

A promise `.catch()` with an empty or comment-only body swallows the error and turns a failure into a feature that quietly never works. A federated-mint 400 rode `.catch(function(){})` on every portal deploys-page load for days; the only symptom was a thing that did not work, and finding it took a trace-ID hunt through the observability lake.
BLOCKING from day one because apps/ is at zero violations. That distinction is the whole point: a gate at zero PREVENTS a regression, while a gate standing over existing violations only decorates them — and a warn-only version of this would emit noise that trains people to skim past harness output, taking the real signals with it.
Deliberately narrow, because each exclusion came from a real occurrence: synchronous `catch (e) {}` is out of scope (eighty-plus exist and many are correct — localStorage probes, ws.close() guards); comments and string literals are blanked before matching, since workspace_deploys.page.html documents this very antipattern in prose and a naive matcher reports the documentation of a rule as a violation of it.
The repair is not "add a comment". Use a forge.flow degrade mode, or a one-line console.debug naming what failed — somewhere a person debugging can actually see it.

Every file under the vendored-JS directory must appear in `manifest.toml` with the sha256 of its bytes, and every declared file must be present and unmodified. Checked in BOTH directions, because they fail differently: the manifest -> disk walk catches tampering and in-place edits, while the disk -> manifest walk catches the file nobody declared — which no manifest-driven check can see, by construction.
That second direction is the one that already bit. forge-portal-web's manifest header has always claimed every vendor file is listed; nothing in the repo enforced it, and an unpinned console script shipped on 22 page templates alongside a byte-identical dead copy of itself, with no build ever objecting.
This duplicates a rule the substrate already implements, and that is a deliberate call rather than an oversight. `forge_web_build::verify_vendor_manifest` is not a verifier: it also writes `asset-manifest.json` and emits `VENDOR_*_HREF` consts, so adopting it means importing an asset-href codegen pipeline the consumer has no use for, and making a repo whose whole purpose is to dogfood the customer surface path-dep the substrate to check its own static files. Roughly thirty lines of hashing, duplicated, buys the check with no build-graph change, no lockfile churn, and no substrate dependency.
BLOCKING from day one, on the same reasoning as no-silent-catch: the tree is at zero violations (all ten files re-hashed clean on 2026-08-09), and a gate that starts at zero PREVENTS a regression, while a gate standing over existing violations only decorates them.
Requires python3 (already a hard dependency of the runner). It does NOT require `tomllib` — that is 3.11+, and the session tier runs on macOS system python 3.9, so the manifest parser is hand-rolled, narrow, and fail-closed: any construct outside `[[dep]]` tables of scalars is exit 2, never a silent skip.

The delta ledger for design-replica work (D-055): while a lane's CURRENT intent has kind design-replica, design/deltas.json must exist, parse, and hold no `open` entries at the done boundary. One entry per reference state x visible attribute (structure, color, weight, spacing, scale, motion, behavior); terminal states are `closed` and `accepted` (with a reason — acceptance without one is how a gap stops being a gap). `open` is the mechanization of "noticed": noticing a delta obligates closing it, and prose cannot fail a gate. Lanes with no replica intent pass with that fact recorded. Pure file parse — deterministic, so it runs unchanged in the CI sweep (no D-012 twin owed).

The paired-state check for design-replica work (D-055): while a lane's CURRENT intent has kind design-replica, every committed reference state (a <state>.png + sidecar in the intent's reference_dir) must have a same-state/viewport/theme capture of OUR converged build, listed in the captures manifest and stamped with the deployed tree's identity — live_hash == desired_hash and git_sha == HEAD. That stamp is the point: a screenshot of an undeployed tree is not evidence (the incident behind this gate produced exactly that false negative), and requiring HEAD forces the honest ordering commit -> push -> converge -> capture -> done. The gate never captures anything itself; the capture script produces the evidence, the gate verifies it. Session-only (ci_skip): captures need a converged local platform. The D-012 CI twin is forge-portal-e2e's capture-parity step (`capture-reference.ts --mode ours --verify-pairs`), which runs the same pairing where the platform exists.

The lintable half of the anti-tell prose doctrine (D-056): prose a human reads must sound like one engineer telling another, and the tells that break that voice — hype vocabulary, "isn't just X" constructions, exclamation marks, emoji, stacked em-dashes — are mechanical enough to grep. This gate scans changed files under the prose roots (marketing content by default): JSON files are parsed and their string values judged (that is where a content model keeps its copy), other text files are scanned as paragraphs. Every hit is reported with its location and the tell it matched; the repair is a rewrite, and the prose-style skill carries the doctrine with worked before/after pairs. The judgment half (rhythm, aphorisms, adjective piles) is prose-review, an LLM judge at pre-review — a grep cannot hear a keynote voice, and pretending it can would make this gate the whole bar.

The generated CMS corpus must match content/** in the same commit. The content pipeline is content/** -> gen_corpus -> the committed domains/content seed -> converge projects it into cms_documents -> the anon render cache invalidates on that table's changelog. Edit content/** without regenerating and every downstream stage reports success while the site serves the old words: in_sync true, live_hash moved, x-forge-cache hit, nothing red anywhere (observed live, 2026-08-18 — the D-056 prose pass deployed cleanly and changed nothing on screen until the corpus was regenerated). ship.sh runs this same preflight, but content-only edits ride a plain git push and never pass through ship.sh — so the guard that "already existed and was wired into NOTHING" (ship.sh's own words) is wired here, at the commit boundary. Consumers without a generated corpus pass with that fact recorded.

verifiers.description: The judgment half of the anti-tell prose doctrine (D-056): a fresh-context judge that reads the diff's prose sentence by sentence against the read-aloud bar — would a senior engineer say this aloud, verbatim, to a peer. Catches what the prose-tells grep cannot: stacked triads, aphoristic closers, adjective piles, uniform rhythm, keynote voice. Blocking at pre-review only — the same dormant-by-default posture D-052 left every judge in; it spends a model call only when a review is explicitly assembled (/harness-review).
